articles.title: The 3-in-1 LEGO Haunted Mansion Drops to a New Low Price, Includes a Haunted Train Build
articles.summary: This year's Labor Day sales have officially begun and the first solid LEGO deal of the week has arrived. The 3-in-1 Haunted Mansion set has dropped to it's lowest price ever on Amazon, now 20% off.
body: If you've been looking for a cool LEGO set to build this Halloween, this discount is absolutely worth a look. As a 3-in-1 set, this Haunted Mansion can also be converted into a Haunted Train or a Haunted ship.

LEGO's Creator line produces some of my favorite sets because of just how versatile these builds are. Right out of the box you can choose to go in three different directions, and each build includes instructions. Seeing as this set is marketed as a Haunted Mansion, that is likely the only build that will use all 736 pieces.

If you do buy this set and only have one specific build in mind, I suggest you start with that one first. I built the 3-in-1 Medieval Horse Knight Castle last year and found it a bit challenging to convert it to a different set once I put together the first one. It's certainly possible, but the instructions for each version of the set include which bag to open next, so once all of the bags are open you're stuck with a big pile of bricks rather than being able to sort everything one bag at a time.

articles.title: Amazon Resale Has a Like New Nintendo Switch Pro Controller for Just $48.12 With Free Shipping
articles.summary: The Switch 2 Pro controller is arguably the best gamepad for the Switch 2 console, but not everyone wants to pay $90 for it. Instead, why not consider the original Switch Pro controller - which has identical build quality and ergonomics and nearly the same feature set - for nearly half the price?
body: Amazon Relsale is selling used "like new" Nintendo Switch Pro controllers for just $48.12 after an automatic 15% discount is applied during checkout. Amazon Resale is Amazon's official outlet for used items. Amazon states that this "Like New" item "looks and functions as if it were new and comes in original packaging." You still get the 30-day Amazon return policy so it's a much safer option than buying a used controller off Facebook Marketplace.

Most importantly, the Switch Pro controller is compatible with the Switch 2. Cosmetically, the Switch Pro and Switch 2 Pro controller look nearly the same apart from the color: the Switch Pro is smoke gray and the Switch 2 Pro is black. Both feature the same excellent build quality and heft that sets this controller apart from most other third party controllers.

articles.title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Beta Extended, Adds Double XP To Help You Grind For Rewards
articles.summary: The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 open beta was supposed to end today, September 1, at 10 AM PT / 1 PM ET, but Activision is extending it. The beta is now set to wrap up at 10 PM PT / 1 AM ET (September 2), meaning it's been extended by a full 12 hours.
body: This is great news for anyone grinding through the levels to claim the MW4 open beta's various rewards. Players who make it all the way to the level cap of 30 get a special weapon blueprint, and now there are 12 more hours to grind for it, or likely less if you're at work, school, eating, sleeping, gardening, etc.

After the beta wraps up, the next time people will be able to play MW4 multiplayer is when the game launches on October 23. The game's single-player campaign, meanwhile, unlocks a week before that for people who preorder.

MW4 is in development for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC. The game is coming to a Nintendo platform for the first time since 2013's Call of Duty: Ghosts. Additionally, MW4 is skipping last-gen consoles for the first time since Ghosts.
The MW4 launch comes 34 days before GTA 6 arrives on November 19.

articles.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Is Leaving Xbox Game Pass This Month
articles.summary: Xbox has announced the latest batch of removals from Game Pass. On Sept. 15, 10 games will leave the service. The biggest name on the list is Cyberpunk 2077; CD Projekt Red's once floundering and now flourishing sci-fi RPG.
body: Cyberpunk 2077 was added in March, so it will have been on the service for only six months. Just last month, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was also removed from Game Pass, perhaps to incentivize players to purchase the upcoming remaster on Sept. 29. As for Cyberpunk 2077, the sequel is a long way off, but a second season of the acclaimed Edgerunners anime is set to be released on Oct. 20 exclusively on Netflix. That will likely boost interest in the game, which CD Projekt Red will want to capitalize on.

The roguelike Metroidvania Dead Cells is another big loss for the service. The 2018 title remains one of the best entries in the popular genre. Fans of Dead Cells will want to keep an eye on developer Evil Empire's next title, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, which will be released on Oct. 15. Spiritfarer, a deeply emotional indie about ferrying the recently deceased to the afterlife, is also worth experiencing before it leaves the service.

articles.title: 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' Breaks Free of Streaming With New Physical Release
articles.summary: Avatar Nation, rise up: Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender is getting a physical release. Paramount Plus and Alliance Home Entertainment announced that the film is coming to DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K Ultra HD. Pre-orders are available now.
body: The film arrived on Paramount Plus on July 24, 2026, to a largely positive reception from fans and critics — it has a 90% critic score and a 99% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. However, even with widespread praise, the movie's release was marred by unfortunate circumstances. In one of the biggest Hollywood leaks in a long time, the entire film was uploaded to X this April after a reported hack.

While Paramount had previously said the movie would launch exclusively on its streaming service, many hoped the leak would push the company to release it theatrically, offering a unique experience compared to watching at home. Unfortunately, the movie only received an extremely limited run in select theaters. At least Paramount is now doing right by the film with a physical release, something that isn’t a given for straight-to-streaming movies. Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender will be released for Blu-ray and DVD on Nov. 3, 2026, and for 4K Ultra HD on Feb. 9, 2027.

articles.title: Double Fine will finally make Brutal Legend 2, but only if its new Kickstarter campaign reaches an almost impossible $100m
articles.summary: Almost two decades on from its first heavy-metal-infused open-world game, Double Fine pinky promises it'll finally make Brutal Legend 2… if the developer's new Kickstarter campaign somehow manages to scrape together $100m (about £74m).
body: Double Fine slid out from under Xbox's ownership earlier this summer, after the console maker kickstarted another round of layoffs affecting 3,200 jobs over the course of the next year. Four Xbox first-party studios also changed ownership, with Double Fine managing to regain both its independence and its entire gameography ( Psychonauts, Kiln, and Brutal Legend included).

Now, the famed developer has returned to Kickstarter to raise money for ' Amnesia Fortnight 2026, Indie Reboot ' - a two-week game jam that'll eventually result in a retail-ready game, plus a behind-the-scenes documentary from the 2 Player Productions crew (of PsychOdyssey fame).

Double Fine's Brutal Legend 2 stretch goal is likely the studio holding onto its signature cheeky humor because, not to burst anyone's bubble, raising $100m on Kickstarter is almost impossible. The most successful Kickstarter campaign of all time raised $46m for a 3D printer. In the video gaming world, Shenmue 3 reigns supreme with a $6m haul.

articles.title: PlayStation argues "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games
articles.summary: As PlayStation's plan to scrap the production of game discs inches closer, Sony's lawyers are arguing that "reasonable consumers" already know that they don't own digital games.
body: This comes in the middle of a class action lawsuit filed against Sony by four customers, who stated back in July that the PlayStation Store's disclosures don't do enough to comply with a certain 2025 California law around digital ownership. Companies are required to let customers know loud and clear that they're not owed access to a digital product forever, even if they've already paid for it, and the claimants feel Sony's not being obvious enough about how digital purchases don't mean digital ownership.
As reported by The Game File, Sony's legal team fired back in a filing from August 21. Sony said most "reasonable consumers would not be misled" by the company's disclosures.

The console maker goes one step further in its argument, alleging that anyone who partakes in digital purchases knows they don't truly own whatever it is they're paying for, because how could more than one person own Resident Evil Requiem otherwise?.
points: As PlayStation's plan to scrap the production of game discs inches closer, Sony's lawyers are arguing that "reasonable consumers" already know that they don't own digital games.

articles.title: CD Projekt Red never considered charging for The Witcher 3 remaster, and says expansion Songs of the Past came from a couple of "happy accidents"
articles.summary: Polish developer CD Projekt Red apparently never considered charging players for the recently revealed Remastered edition of The Witcher 3, and it has explained more about how the expansion Songs of the Past came to be, citing a couple of "happy accidents".
body: The Remastered edition of The Witcher 3, revealed at Gamescom last week, significantly overhauls the now 11-year-old role-playing game, not only visually, but also from a gameplay point of view, addressing its much-maligned combat but also enemy behaviour, horse riding, skill trees, and more. Yet despite all of the apparent work that's gone into it, it's going to be a free upgrade for everyone who owns the game.

Charging for it? "I don't think it was ever a thought we even had," CD Projekt Red joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski told The Game Business. "It was never a question we asked ourselves." Instead, CD Projekt Red thought about it as an improvement and a way to introduce the expansion Songs of the Past.

"I remember we were going deeper and deeper into the development of Songs of the Past with Fool's Theory and we started chatting, like, 'Why don't we make the game more modern? Everything feels like it was developed 10 years ago.' And that was really the beginning of the conversation. And we started chatting, like, 'What could we do to improve it?'
